title: Can Convert String in K Moves
summary: Given two strings s and t , determine if it is possible to convert s into t in no more than k moves.
statement: Given two strings s and t , determine if it is possible to convert s into t in no more than k moves. In each move i (where 1 ≤ i ≤ k ), you can choose any index j (1-indexed) from s that has not been chosen in any previous move, and shift the character at that index i times. Shifting a character by i means applying the shift operation i times, with the alphabet wrapping around if necessary. An index can be chosen at most once per move. Return true if the conversion is possible within the given moves, otherwise return false.
constraints: Move i can shift one not-yet-chosen index forward by i letters modulo 26; each index is used at most once.
Return whether all required shifts can be assigned distinct move numbers no greater than k.
hints: Compute each position’s forward shift modulo 26; zero needs no move.
The first occurrence of shift d uses move d, the next d+26, then d+52, and so on.
Track how many times each shift has appeared and reject if its required move exceeds k.
These are the earliest distinct moves producing that residue, so any later schedule cannot improve feasibility.
